title: [gRPC Python] Stop using unstable Cython versions
body:
### What version of gRPC and what language are you using?
Python with gRPC 1.70.0/1.71.0/1.72.0, but the version is irrelevant

### What operating system (Linux, Windows,...) and version?
Windows & Linux & macOS

### What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g. python version or version of gcc)
Python 3.12.10, but that's irrelevant

### What did you do?
`pip install grpcio==<version>`

macOS killed my async Python gRPC server after 1 minute, since it was using 100 GB of memory.
Tried the same code on Linux with the same gRPC version, and it worked fine.
After a long investigation, it turns out this is neither my bug nor your bug nor macOS's fault, it's a [Cython bug](https://github.com/cython/cython/issues/6878), because `grpcio==1.71.0` was built with `Cython==3.1.0a1` which is an unstable unreleased alpha version of Cython. Additionally, it only happens on macOS because the same gRPC version is built using different Cython versions for each OS.

### What did you expect to see?
gRPC uses Cython, so I expected stable gRPC to use stable released Cython versions, not alpha and beta versions.
Also, I expected the Cython versions to be constant across different operating systems.

Using an unstable version of Cython in a stable version of gRPC doesn't make sense to me - it means you'll likely have bugs that will be fixed when it releases, and I don't think you gain anything from using unstable versions.

I think that using unstable Cython in unstable gRPC is still weird, but might make sense if you want your latest version to use the latest Cython version. I think it's best to always use stable Cython versions, so that bugs reported about your release candidates will be your bugs and not Cython bugs. If you're worried about Cython affecting you in weird ways, maybe your stable version should always use a month-old stable Cython version, and use the latest stable Cython only in rc versions.

Using different Cython versions for different operating systems with the same gRPC version is annoying, it means that I can't expect the same behavior from the same code running on different operating systems.
I also see no reason for this, although I think it's less of a worry than using unstable versions.

### What did you see instead?
I checked every wheel on pypi for these versions:
- `grpcio==1.71.0` is built with:
    - `Cython==3.0.12` on Windows
    - `Cython==3.0.11` on Linux
    - `Cython==3.1.0a1` on macOS (unstable alpha pre-release)
- `grpcio==1.72.0rc1` is weirder:
  - `Cython==3.1.0b1` on macOS
  - `Cython==3.1.0a1` on Linux `manylinux_2_17_aarch64`
  - `Cython==3.0.12` on the rest of Linux (`musllinux_1_1_aarch64` and all non-aarch64 variants)
  - `Cython==3.0.12` on Windows

### Anything else we should know about your project / environment?
I also checked `grpcio==1.70.0` and it's always `Cython==3.0.11` which is great.
I didn't check earlier versions than that.

To check the Cython version of an installed grpc: `print(type(grpc._cython.cygrpc.execute_batch))`

You can also `grep` for the version inside the compiled binary inside the wheel, which is what I did to test every wheel (otherwise I'd need a lot of weird OSes and Python versions). I grepped for `_cython_(\w+)\.cython_function_or_method`.
